summary: The drop-in authoring surface is cured end to end on the data-row path and the recorded placement frame is generalized from the pure-z `rz` rotation to a full orthonormal 3x3 frame: `world = translate(o) ∘ R ∘ M` with volume invariant under R (exact, never recomputed), the world bbox the AABB of the 8 rotated local corners, and the mesh transformed per-vertex; the coordinate-plane `mirror` semantics stay byte-identical (the pure-z rows keep the recorded `rz` path bit-for-bit). The kernel PartSpec gains an optional `rotation` (x_dir/y_dir/z_dir) column frame beside the legacy `rz` field, so every existing row (JSON and Rust) parses unchanged and no green row changes verdict. The four named tests are green: placed-frame rigidity (a solid under an arbitrary orthonormal frame equals the unplaced facts volume-wise exactly and bbox-wise as the rotated AABB), a Plane-frame extrude answering world facts, a Pos-placed multi-solid assembly reporting placed solid_count, and the Vector direction-math surface answering client-side. The corpus door's shim stubs flip to recorded data rows name-for-name: `Vector` gains normalized/dot/cross/length and the scalar/difference arithmetic; `Plane(origin, x_dir, z_dir)` and the `Plane.XY/XZ/YZ` markers record an orthonormal frame (fixed-order orthonormalization, y = z cross x) with `.offset` composing a normal translation; `Pos` records a translation frame; `Rotation`/`Rot` record an Euler frame; `Location` generalizes beyond translation/pure-z to the same frame data; `Plane * face`/`Plane * part` placement algebra records rows; `Spline`/`Line`/`Polyline`/`Polygon` build profile data rows; and the framed drop-in exposes the census placement vocabulary with typed refusals for genuinely open carriers (spline-section lofts, spline-trimmed extrudes, non-z revolve axes, partial arcs, boolean ops, OCC-only probes of data rows) - never approximated, never an untyped authoring failure. The kernel-door smoke census over all 21 F1 rows (kernel engine only, one fresh python per row, serial) records per-row verdicts: 0 untyped authoring DNFs remain (the 9 Vector-surface rows and the 12 typed-stub rows all flip to real verdicts), and the measured boundary deepened for every row - rows stop TYPED at their first boolean op (airbox, details), at an open authoring carrier (the four wheel-corner rows at the wheel-frame non-z revolve, rear_wing/steering_rack/suspension_front/suspension_rear at the spline-trimmed extrude), at the OCC-only bound probe (engine_cover, monocoque), or at the kernel facts/export arm over recorded out-of-envelope carriers (the spline-section-loft rows). No F1 row returned green geometry facts: the corpus's F1 parts are all spline-section lofts / revolved-about-the-axle / booleans, so zero rows reduce to the canonical envelope; per scope 2/3 the boolean boundary rows and the open-carrier rows are successful deepenings, recorded as the next boundary. OCC references are untouched (not re-run per the packet - the references were verified bit-identical at TTC-RECENSUS-F1).

implementation.bridge_types: truck123d/src/bd_bridge.rs: PartSpec gains `rotation: Option<RotationFrame>` (serde-defaulted, skip-serializing; `RotationFrame { x_dir, y_dir, z_dir }` columns = the world images of the part-local axes). `RotationFrame::apply` maps a local point through the recorded orthonormal matrix. `part_world_bbox` and the STL mesh path branch: a recorded frame replaces the pure-z path exactly (the AABB of the 8 rotated local corners / per-vertex triangle transform); rows without a frame keep the existing `rz` cos/sin path byte-identical. `mirror` semantics unchanged (mirror applies to the local geometry before the rotation and translation; the pure-z mirror test stays bit-identical).
implementation.frame_policy: Volume is computed from the unplaced solid only (placement never recomputes volume, so it is invariant under any orthonormal R by construction); the world bbox is the AABB of the 8 rotated local corners; the mesh transforms per vertex. Placement never changes a carrier class and never participates in admission.
implementation.door_recording: corpus/ttc/door.py: `Vector` now answers the full corpus direction-math surface (normalized, dot, cross, length, scalar mult/div both sides, difference, unary minus, .X/.Y/.Z, iteration) as pure client-side data. Placement frames are a single `_Frame` model (origin + orthonormal columns) shared by `Plane` (keyword or positional `origin`/`x_dir`/`z_dir`, fixed-order orthonormalization, markers `Plane.XY/XZ/YZ`, `.rotated` and `.offset`), `Pos` (translation), `Location` (translation or Euler rotation), `Rotation`/`Rot` (Euler), and `Axis`. Frames multiply shapes on the left (`frame * shape`): Face/Wire/Edge boundary points are transformed (data), `_Part` frames compose (`_locate_in_place` for the method path keeps the pure-z `rz` accumulation byte-identical), and `Compound`/lists place recursively. Profile carriers `Spline`/`Line` build recorded edges, `Polygon`/`Polyline` build line-edge wires, and `make_face` faces any closed wire; `Circle` keeps a typed refusal naming the open circle-profile carrier. `extrude`/`revolve`/`loft` record rows (loft records spline-section faces and the kernel refuses their exact smooth volume at the facts arm), booleans (+, -, &, fuse, cut) and fillet/chamfer refuse TYPED naming the op, and an OCC-only probe of a data row (`.wrapped`) refuses typed instead of passing None into OCP.
implementation.kernel_tests: Four tests added in truck123d/src/bd_bridge.rs mod tests: placed_frame_facts_match_unplaced_facts_under_rigid_motion (pure Rust, JSON-submitted frame row), plane_frame_extrude_answers_world_facts / pos_placed_assembly_counts_solids / vector_surface_answers_direction_math (door rows built in a real python -c process and measured through the native `tree_facts` arm; the door surface is pure client data so no module staging is needed).

After this packet every row reaches a real verdict: 0 untyped DNFs; airbox/details reach the boolean boundary; the corner rows reach the wheel-frame revolve; rear_wing/steering_rack/suspension rows reach the spline-trimmed extrude; the bodywork rows build their spline-section lofts and stop typed at the facts/STL arm, at the corpus OCC-probe/validation helpers, or at the spline-trimmed extrude. findings.title: No F1 row is fully green: the corpus's F1 parts are all outside the canonical facts envelope, so the census boundary is typed by construction
findings.detail: The 21 F1 rows build their geometry from spline-section body lofts (bodywork shells), axle-revolved profiles about the wheel-frame non-z axis, spline-trimmed extrudes, or boolean products. None of those reduce to the canonical envelope rows the executor measures exactly, so zero rows return geometry facts equal to a reference - every row stops TYPED at its first boolean, at an open authoring carrier, or at the kernel facts/STL arm. This is the scope-2/scope-3 expected deepening (a row reaching the boolean is a successful deepening, not a failure); the per-row verdicts are recorded in the census above.

findings.title: The two body-loft rows (floor, diffuser) and the two OCC-bound-probe rows (engine_cover, monocoque) stop at corpus validation helpers, not at a kernel refusal
findings.detail: floor/diffuser abort inside the corpus `_loft_stack` validation wrapper (surfaces.is_valid_shape on a data-only loft returns False, so every trial is rejected and the corpus raises its own RuntimeError 'floor loft failed: None'). engine_cover/monocoque reach the corpus's OCC-only bound probes (surfaces.bbox/obox) on the recorded data rows; those now refuse TYPED ('.wrapped' raises a typed refusal instead of passing None into OCP, which previously died as an untyped TypeError). The two RuntimeError rows carry typed corpus exceptions (no untyped authoring failure); recorded verbatim.
